body:
YouTube embeds fail with Error 153 ("Video player configuration error") in ALL of filemark's non-web hosts — chrome-extension://, vscode-webview://, file:// — because YouTube requires a valid http(s) Referer those origins can't send. It is a referrer/handshake failure, NOT a per-video permission issue (playableInEmbed:true is irrelevant; 150/101 are the real "embedding disabled" codes). Vimeo/Loom have no such requirement.
Fix (live 2026-08-09): route YouTube through a tiny https helper page at apps/website/public/embed/youtube.html -> https://khanakia.com/apps/filemark/embed/youtube.html?v=<id>. It reads ?v=, sets <meta name="referrer" content="strict-origin-when-cross-origin">, and iframes youtube-nocookie; the non-web host iframes THIS page so YouTube sees a khanakia.com Referer and plays. A srcdoc/data: shim does NOT work (inherits null origin). Code: packages/mdx-viewer/src/components/VideoEmbed.tsx (parseVideo/youtubeNeedsHelper/youtubeHelperUrl/resolveIframeSrc) + an iframe component override in MDXViewer.tsx (reroutes raw pasted <iframe> too). On the website (https) it embeds directly.
Three header/CSP gotchas, in the order they bit (all required): (1) VS Code webview CSP (default-src 'none') must add `frame-src https://khanakia.com` (apps/vscode/src/extension.ts VIDEO_EMBED_ORIGINS) or the iframe is blank. (2) The helper must be framable cross-origin, but the site-wide `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` in apps/website/_headers blocks it — exempt /apps/filemark/embed/* with `! X-Frame-Options`. (3) CSP `frame-ancestors *` does NOT cover chrome-extension:// (the wildcard matches only network schemes http/https/ws/wss); listing explicit schemes fixes Chrome but NOT the VS Code webview, whose sandboxed/OPAQUE (null) origin no frame-ancestors token can allowlist — so the final fix is to send NO frame-ancestors at all on /embed/* (just drop XFO), making it framable everywhere. Safe: the page only wraps a public video.
